questions.question: Why do Catholics pray to Mary?
questions.answer: Catholics don't worship Mary, but honor her and ask for her intercession. Just as we ask friends to pray for us, we ask Mary to pray for us.

scriptures.text: At the wedding at Cana, Mary intercedes for the couple: 'They have no wine.' Then she tells the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you.'
Mary herself prophesies: 'All generations will call me blessed.'
The dragon is angry with the woman (Mary) and goes off to wage war on 'the rest of her offspring'—those who keep God's commandments.

questions.question: Where is the Catholic Church in the Bible?
questions.answer: Jesus established the Church with Peter as its foundation and gave it authority to teach and forgive sins.

scriptures.text: Jesus said: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven.'
Paul calls the Church 'the pillar and foundation of truth.'
Jesus breathed on them and said: 'Receive the Holy Spirit. Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them.'

questions.question: How should I pray when I feel distant from God?
questions.answer: Even when we feel dry in prayer, God is still present. Persist in prayer and trust that God hears you.

scriptures.text: Even Jesus quoted this: 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me? O my God, I cry by day, but you do not answer.'
The Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit intercedes for us.
Jesus told them a parable about the need to pray always and not lose heart.

questions.question: How do I resist temptation?
questions.answer: Through prayer, Scripture, and the sacraments, especially Confession and the Eucharist.

scriptures.text: No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation he will also provide the way of escape.
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

questions.question: Why is faith alone not enough for salvation?
questions.answer: Faith is essential for salvation, but it must be accompanied by works. True faith produces good works as its fruit. At the end of the day, the devil also believes in God, but that faith does not save him. It's what he does with that faith that matters. What matters most is you're striving to achieve your faith through your works. Your works are a reflection of your faith and your commitment to living out that faith in your daily life, but don't be confused with the idea or assumption that your works is what the Lord cares about alone. The thief on the cross sinned his entire life, yet he was promised paradise because of his faith. He was the only one willing to die with Jesus, which shows that not only faith is the key, but his works as well. Because the thief truly believed in our Lord, Jesus Christ, he died with Him, which showcased his true works as well as his unwavering faith.

scriptures.text: So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.

For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.

questions.question: If God is all-powerful, why does he allow suffering?
questions.answer: God allows suffering for reasons that are often beyond our understanding. It can lead to spiritual growth, compassion, and a deeper relationship with Him. Suffering can also be a test of our faith and character.

scriptures.text: Not only that, but we rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our affliction.
Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.
The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

questions.question: How can a loving God send anyone to Hell?
questions.answer: God's desire is for all to be saved, but He respects our free will. Hell is a consequence of rejecting God's love and mercy. Meaning, we choose our eternal destiny through our actions and choices in this life.

scriptures.text: The Lord is not slow to fulfill his promise as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.
Then he will say to those on his left, 'Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.'
And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.

questions.question: Can my works soley get me into heaven?
questions.answer: No, salvation is a gift from God that we receive through faith in Jesus Christ and His grace. While good works are important and demonstrate our faith, they cannot earn us salvation on their own. Works are only the fruit of your faith, the Lord does not care for any of your works on Earth. You must have faith in Him, works are only a benefactor of that faith, your works is what separates you from the devil. The devil has faith in the Lord as well, but that faith does not save him because of how he chooses to act on his faith.

scriptures.text: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.
He saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to his own mercy.
Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure.

questions.question: How can I combat Lustful thoughts?
questions.answer: This is a common misconception in the bible, as nowhere in it does it state that lustful thoughts or actions are fended by combat. The Lord calls you to flee from lust, not to fight it. How that may look may vary, but it is important to remember that you are not alone in this struggle and that God's grace is sufficient to help you overcome temptation.

scriptures.text: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

questions.question: Can we trust the bible is true and not corrupted?
questions.answer: Yes, we can trust that the Bible is true and has been preserved from corruption. The Bible has been carefully transmitted through generations, and the core message of salvation through Jesus Christ remains intact. The Bible was written by 40 different authors over a span of 1,500 years, yet it maintains a consistent message and theme throughout.

scriptures.text: The sum of your word is truth, and every one of your righteous rules endures forever.
Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.

questions.question: Was Jesus a Jew?
questions.answer: Yes, Jesus was a Jew both ethnically and religiously. He was born into a Jewish family, observed Jewish customs, and taught in synagogues. However, Jesus believed in the laws of Moses, like the pharises. He did not come to abolish the law or just follow it, but to fulfill it, unlike all Jews at the time who simply followed it.

scriptures.text: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.
And at the end of eight days, when he was circumcised, he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.
For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Who are the true children of God?
questions.answer: The true children of God are those who believe in Jesus Christ and follow His teachings. They are born of God and live according to His will. This is often confused with physical descent, but spiritual descent through faith is what truly matters. The people who live in Israel at the time of Jesus were not considered the true children of God because they rejected Him as the Messiah.

scriptures.text: But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God.
For in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith.
For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

But he replied to the man who told him, 'Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?' And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, 'Here are my mother and my brothers! For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.'

questions.question: How can I overcome past sin?
questions.answer: Overcoming past sin involves sincere repentance, seeking God's forgiveness, and making amends where possible. It is important to remember that God's grace is sufficient to cover all sins, and through faith in Jesus Christ, we can be made new. Jesus even stated that He came to call sinners, not the righteous, and even forgets our sins when we repent.

scriptures.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
'Come now, let us reason together,' says the Lord. 'Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.'
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.

questions.question: How can I align work with faith?
questions.answer: You can align your work with your faith by viewing your job as am opportunity to serve others, just as Jesus did. Seek every instance in a way to glorify Him in everything you do.

scriptures.text: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You are serving the Lord Christ.
So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
Rendering service with a good will as to the Lord and not to men, knowing that whatever good anyone does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether he is a bondservant or is free.

questions.question: What does it mean to be religious and why do I have to be religious?
questions.answer: A lot of people believe being religious means following a set of rules or rituals, but at its core, being religious is about having a relationship with God and living according to His will. It involves faith, worship, and moral living. Being religious helps us grow closer to God, find purpose in life, and live in a way that reflects His love and teachings. It's also a beautiful, natural way to communicate with others who share your beliefs, fostering a sense of community and support.

scriptures.text: Religion that is pure and undefiled before God, the Father, is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.

And he said to him, 'You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.' This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'

questions.question: I'm new to my faith, how or where should I start learning?
questions.answer: Starting your faith journey can be both exciting and overwhelming. A good starting point is to read the Bible, beginning with the Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John) to learn about the life and teachings of Jesus Christ. Additionally, consider joining a local church or faith community where you can connect with others, attend services, and participate in study groups. Don't hesitate to ask questions and seek guidance from more experienced believers or clergy members. Prayer is also essential; ask God for wisdom and understanding as you grow in your faith. Social events like Youth Groups or Bible Studies can also be great ways to learn and connect with others on the same journey. Just remember, you're not alone, and God is with you every step of the way.

scriptures.text: All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.

And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

questions.question: How can I hear God's voice?
questions.answer: Hearing God's voice often requires quieting our minds and hearts to be receptive to His guidance. This can be achieved through regular prayer, meditation on Scripture, and spending time in silence. God may speak to us through the Bible, through the counsel of wise believers, or through a sense of peace about a decision. It's important to be patient and open, as God's timing and methods may differ from our expectations.

scriptures.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
Be still, and know that I am God.
And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, 'This is the way, walk in it,' when you turn to the right or when you turn to the left.

questions.question: Why are there so many denominations?
questions.answer: The existence of many denominations within Christianity can be attributed to a variety of factors, including differing interpretations of Scripture, cultural influences, historical events, and theological disagreements. As the Church has grown and spread across different regions and cultures, various groups have emerged, each emphasizing different aspects of the faith. While this diversity can lead to confusion, it also reflects the richness of the Christian tradition and the ways in which the Gospel can be understood and lived out in different contexts.

scriptures.text: I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same judgment.

There is one body and one Spirit—just as you were called to the one hope that belongs to your call—one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
As for the one who is weak in faith, welcome him, but not to quarrel over opinions.

questions.question: How do I align faith and my relationship to the person I love?
questions.answer: The most important aspect of building faith into your relationship is the foundation being the Lord. Nothing good will come from it if there is a division in one partner from the Lord, once the Lord sees said division, he will not bless the relationship. Pray together, attend church together, and discuss your faith openly to ensure you are both on the same page spiritually. This shared spiritual foundation can strengthen your bond and help you navigate challenges together.

scriptures.text: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, with thankfulness in your hearts to God.

questions.question: What is the difference between a pastor, preist, and preacher?
questions.answer: A pastor is a general term for a spiritual leader who shepherds a congregation, often used in Protestant denominations. A priest is a specific role in the Catholic, Orthodox, and some Anglican churches, responsible for administering sacraments and leading worship. A preacher is someone who delivers sermons or messages, which can be a role held by pastors, priests, or other religious leaders.

scriptures.text: Shepherd the flock of God that is among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion, but willingly, as God would have you; not for shameful gain, but eagerly; not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock.

Every high priest chosen from among men is appointed to act on behalf of men in relation to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins. He can deal gently with the ignorant and wayward, since he himself is beset with weakness. Because of this he is obligated to offer sacrifice for his own sins just as he does for those of the people. And no one takes this honor for himself, but only when called by God, just as Aaron was.

How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, 'How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!'

questions.question: Is drinking a sin?
questions.answer: First thing to ask yourself is why? Drinking isn't inherently a sin, however, when done excessively or in a way that leads to harm or impairs judgment, it can become sinful. The Bible warns against drunkenness and encourages moderation. The reason why it then becomes a question of why am I doing it is because if you're drinking to the point of excess or to escape reality, then that is where it becomes a sin as well. Intent and moderation are key factors in determining whether drinking is sinful.

scriptures.text: And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit.
Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.
'All things are lawful for me,' but not all things are helpful. 'All things are lawful for me,' but I will not be dominated by anything.

questions.question: What does the Bible say about mental health?
questions.answer: The Bible acknowledges the reality of mental and emotional struggles and offers comfort, hope, and guidance for those facing such challenges. It encourages believers to cast their anxieties on God, seek peace through prayer, and find strength in His presence. The Bible also emphasizes the importance of community, support, and caring for one another in times of distress.

scriptures.text: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
When the righteous cry for help, the Lord hears and delivers them out of all their troubles. The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

questions.question: Is it a sin to smoke weed/nicotine?
questions.answer: While the bible does not explicitly mention smoking weed or nicotine, it does provide principles that can be applied to this question. The body is considered a temple of the Holy Spirit, and believers are encouraged to honor God with their bodies. If smoking leads to addiction, harms health, or impairs judgment, it can be seen as dishonoring to God. Additionally, anything that hinders our ability to serve God and others effectively should be approached with caution. For medicinal purposes are completely different, as the Bible encourages us to seek healing and care for our bodies. All in all, moderation and intent are once again the key factors that play into whether smoking is sinful or not.

scriptures.text: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.
Be sober-minded; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
'All things are lawful for me,' but not all things are helpful. 'All things are lawful for me,' but I will not be dominated by anything.
No longer drink only water, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments.

questions.question: What are the seven deadly sins?
questions.answer: The seven deadly sins, also known as the capital vices or cardinal sins, are a classification of vices in Christian teaching. They are: 1) Pride, 2) Greed, 3) Lust, 4) Envy, 5) Gluttony, 6) Wrath, and 7) Sloth. These sins are considered to be the root causes of other sins and immoral behavior. They are often contrasted with the seven heavenly virtues, which are humility, charity, chastity, gratitude, temperance, patience, and diligence.

scriptures.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils. It is through this craving that some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pangs.
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

questions.question: Is starving yourself considered a sin?
questions.answer: Starving oneself can be considered a sin if it is done out of pride, self-hatred, or a desire to control one's body in a way that dishonors God. The Bible teaches that our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit and should be treated with respect and care. However, fasting for spiritual purposes, such as seeking God's guidance or growing closer to Him, is encouraged in Scripture. The key distinction lies in the intent behind the action.

scriptures.text: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

And when you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces that their fasting may be seen by others. Truly, I say to you, they have received their reward. But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, that your fasting may not be seen by others but by your Father who is in secret. And your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
Oh, taste and see that the Lord is good! Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him!

questions.question: Is it a sin to fight in self-defense?
questions.answer: It is not a sin when the intention is to protect oneself or others from harm. The Bible acknowledges the right to self-defense, as seen in various passages where individuals defend themselves or others. However, it is important to ensure that the response is proportionate to the threat and that the intention is not driven by anger, revenge, or a desire to harm others unnecessarily.

scriptures.text: If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him, but if the sun has risen on him, there shall be bloodguilt for him. He shall surely pay. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

And I looked and arose and said to the nobles and to the officials and to the rest of the people, 'Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes.'
Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Be careful to do what is right in the eyes of everyone. If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.

questions.question: Are christians better than those who don't believe?
questions.answer: Christians are not better in anyway shape or form, in most cases they may even be worse. The Bible teaches that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. Salvation is available to all through faith in Jesus Christ, regardless of one's background or beliefs. Christians are called to love and serve others humbly, recognizing their own need for God's grace. The reason why in some circumstances Christians may actually be worse is because they hold themselves to a higher standard, and when they fail to meet that standard, it can lead to greater condemnation. It's the fact that a Christian knows better, yet still sins, that makes their judgement stricter.

scriptures.text: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
Judge not, that you be not judged. For with the judgment you pronounce you will be judged, and with the measure you use it will be measured to you.

Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven. On that day many will say to me, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?' And then will I declare to them, 'I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of iniquity.'

questions.question: What does it mean to be a believer vs a disciple of christ? Is there a difference?
questions.answer: The word disciple comes from the Greek word 'mathetes,' which means 'learner' or 'student.' A believer is someone who has faith in Jesus Christ as their Lord and Savior, accepting His teachings and the salvation He offers. A disciple, on the other hand, goes beyond mere belief; they actively follow Jesus' teachings, seek to live according to His example, and commit to spreading His message. In essence, all disciples are believers, but not all believers are disciples. Being a disciple involves a deeper level of commitment and action in one's faith journey. Some characteristics of a disciple include, but aren't limited to: abiding to His word, denying oneself, loving one another, and bearing fruit.

scriptures.text: So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him, 'If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples.'
And he said to all, 'If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.'

A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.
By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and so prove to be my disciples.
